fixes.R2f1: Handoff identity/ownership: recorded exact repair-2 base, repair-1 tip, implementation head/tree, per-commit SHAs, changed files and verification. The two already-adapted P10/P12W test paths (app_test.go, rollback_fence_test.go) were re-declared as owned by this repair boundary; no change was needed to them. No path outside the exhaustive boundary changed: no migrations, frozen contracts/manifests, traversal/stun/udp libraries, docs, configs or other worktrees.
fixes.R2f2: Auto strategy correctness: resolveAutoStrategy walks the CURRENT configured AutoOrder and accepts only a matching PASSED profile result (Profile.DefaultStrategy is a diagnostic/cache field, never an order authority); UDP auto resolves to direct-v4 BEFORE the TCP detection profile is loaded/validated (a stale/malformed/absent TCP profile cannot affect UDP); fixed non-direct UDP strategies fail closed instead of being silently rewritten; a present profile without a network fingerprint is refused as stale. AutoOrder is normalized into a.cfg before composition so rebuildTraversal preserves it.
fixes.R2f3: Nil managers: manual-static and explicit-gateway selected routes with a nil Plain/Gateway Manager return ordinary errors instead of panicking; direct-v4 stays manager-free.
fixes.R2f4: Generation fencing: every actor stamps compositionGeneration/capabilityGeneration/route fingerprint before the external acquisition (newForwardActorResolved from the resolved route; newUDPActor from a fresh snapshot). capabilityGeneration bumps on every loss/restore transition and compositionGeneration on every rebuild. apply and finishReopen re-check the fence under the install lock and refuse to publish an actor built against an obsolete composition; the acquisition is abandoned with ownership retained.
fixes.R2f5: Same-Forward serialization: beginForwardOperation serializes route resolution + external acquisition + install per ForwardID (independent forwards stay concurrent). Deterministic tests prove a concurrent apply never starts a second acquisition and an apply-vs-reopen race runs exactly one Map.
fixes.R2f6: Composition snapshot and UPnP ownership: composeTraversal gives the plain Manager, gateway Manager and Detector each an independent adapter map (newMappers x3) so a mutable UPnP adapter is never shared across owners; rebuildTraversal publishes PlainManager/GatewayManager/Detector/StunObserver/StunSource together and bumps compositionGeneration.
fixes.R2f7: Cleanup/retry/recovery: abandonAcquiredActor retains cleanup ownership (cleanupPending + drain) and tears down with a detached bounded context, so a canceled caller can never strand a listener/mapping. OnActorCleaned fires after a successful non-delete cleanup and the app schedules a bounded recover so a forward stranded by capability loss reopens without a new route change. FIXED a pre-existing latent double-close that stranded every gateway actor in cleanupPending forever: the wrapped tcp.Forward and the manager acquisition own the same listener; cleanupActor now treats an EXCLUSIVELY redundant net.ErrClosed release error (exclusiveErrClosed) as clean, while a real mapping/journal failure still keeps the actor owned. Acquisition.Release is sync.Once and is never claimed to retry after a real release failure (truthful pending state; the durable journal record is the retained evidence).
fixes.R2f8: Lifecycle/probe deletion-window fence: onMappingLifecycle and applyProbeOutcome re-check the durable delete fence under the admission ordering so a trailing lifecycle/probe event cannot recreate activation state after a forward is deleted. Mutable acquisition metadata reads remain the documented benign monotone/immutable reads (repair R1 finding 9); no traversal API redesign, D5 residual documented.

known_limits_added_this_cycle: A manager acquisition whose Release genuinely fails (e.g. a mapper Delete adapter error) stays owned in cleanupPending; Acquisition.Release is sync.Once and is intentionally never claimed to retry — the durable journal record is the retained evidence that the gateway mapping may still be live. This matches the repair-2 finding-7 guidance and is not a regression.
govulncheck is not installed in this worktree, so vulnerability scanning remains unexecuted (same caveat as prior cycles).

The repair-2 deletion-window fence closes lifecycle/probe events against a durable delete fence; the residual D5 callback-token replacement window (a trailing OnMapping* event satisfying a live replacement forward's mapped guard) is unchanged and still documented.
